notes:
Background: Argus powers a white‑label contact center platform used by ~1,200 enterprise merchants. 24/7 global support for merchants is core to product. Recently customers demanded more automated agent assist and faster ticket summarization to reduce AHT.

Key asks from call: dedicated capacity (reserved GPU/throughput) for predictable latency during global sale days; strict isolation/VPC + KMS; EU data residency for European merchant tenants. Wants SLA-backed p95 latency targets during spikes.

POC scope: connect to staging Zendesk + Argus agent desktop; validate tool-calling to internal CASE API (create/update ticket, escalate); run synthetic spike tests simulating 1,500 concurrent agents and 30% bot-augmented interactions. Success criteria: p95 token latency within agreed SLO, <5% error rate on tool-calls, summaries meet F1 threshold on internal eval set.

Quotes / snippets: "We need predictable performance on Black Friday — outages or throttling cost us real revenue." AE notes: procurement focused on committed cost vs. burst pricing. SE notes: prioritize KV cache for short conversational history and deterministic rollbacks for tool-calls.

Integration notes: primary agent desktop = Argus Desk (custom), CRM = Zendesk (primary) + Salesforce (pilot). Agent workflow requires direct tool-calling hooks (create ticket, attach summarization, run triage script).

Risks called out: hallucination on sensitive fields, retry semantics for failed tool-calls, model regression at quantization. Legal asks for clear retention and deletion paths for EU tenant data.

Stubs/links: pricing deck + security answers uploaded to Drive, threads in Gmail for procurement. Jira tickets created for POC infra questions (RDW-3124, RDW-3250).
requirements_summary: Enterprise contact center vendor looking for Redwood Dedicated: reserved throughput across NA+EU regions, VPC isolation, KMS integration, audit logging, SLA for peak sale-day spikes. Must support Zendesk and agent-desktop tool-calls with < 1s end-user latency for common agent-assist flows; able to fall back to smaller model variants on overload. POC to validate latency+reliability and tool-call idempotency.
